title: Candlelight vigil in Mumbai for deceased IIT Bombay student
seoTitle: Mumbai vigil for IIT Bombay student

tea.why: People gathered for a candlelight vigil following the death of an IIT Bombay student amid allegations of caste-based discrimination.
tea.want: Demanding justice for the deceased student, an impartial investigation, the arrest of accused professors, and the resignation of the IIT Bombay director.
tea.changed: Oct 25: Mumbai Police detained around 140 participants across two locations for holding unauthorised candlelight vigils.

summary: On October 25, 2026, protesters and student groups gathered in Mumbai for candlelight vigils to demand justice following the death of an IIT Bombay student, Sahil Wakode, who died by suicide last month after facing alleged caste-based harassment. Organised in part by groups such as the Progressive Students Union and 'Adivasi Gen Z', the participants called for an impartial probe, the arrest of involved professors, and the resignation of the IIT Bombay director. Mumbai Police intervened, citing a lack of required permissions, and detained approximately 140 individuals across Chaityabhoomi in Dadar and Shivaji Park, including comedian Masoom Rajwani. Police stated that precautionary measures were taken to maintain order, and those detained were subsequently released later that evening.
demands: Impartial investigation into the student death
Resignation of the IIT Bombay director
response: Mumbai Police detained approximately 140 protesters at Chaityabhoomi and Shivaji Park for participating in unauthorised gatherings, stating precautionary measures were necessary to maintain law and order. Those detained were released later that evening. Police did not respond to allegations of manhandling.

arrests.text: Around 140 people were detained by Mumbai Police across Chaityabhoomi and Shivaji Park.

updates.text: Mumbai Police detained around 140 protesters participating in unauthorised candlelight vigils at Chaityabhoomi and Shivaji Park.
